correctness.rationale: For each commutative chain ring \(S\) of length \(k\), every primitive \(2\times2\) square-zero matrix \(Y\) is conjugate to the rank-one Jordan nilpotent: \((Yv,v)\) is a basis. Its invertible centralizer has \((q^k-q^{k-1})q^k\) elements, giving \((q^2-1)q^{2k-2}\) primitive matrices. At valuation \(s<\lceil d/2\rceil\), reduction to length \(d-2s\) and \(q^{4s}\) lifts give \((q^2-1)q^{2d-2}\) matrices, independent of the shell. Matrices in the deep ideal \((\pi^{\lceil d/2\rceil})\) are automatically square-zero, exactly \(q^{4\lfloor d/2\rfloor}\) of them. A bounded deep-to-shell mass ratio proves weak convergence to the uniform distribution on \([0,1/2]\). The bundled checker exhaustively verifies twenty finite examples, including characteristic two, nonprime residue size four and mixed characteristic.

originality.rationale: The inspected motivating centralizer classification arXiv:2212.08425 classifies realizable Jordan partitions, not counts of square-zero matrices by entry-minimum pi-adic valuation. The ring-wide uniform shell formula and fixed-\(q\) limit do not follow from the referenced existence statements. Sources concerning traceless matrix enumeration and squarefree polynomial equations address different conditions. Published results may still contain an equivalent local-orbit formula: search nonappearance is not a uniqueness certificate, and incomplete access to an older index-counting paper is disclosed.
residual_risks: A mathematically equivalent valuation-refined count may exist under the language of similarity classes over local principal ideal rings or nilpotent matrix orbits.

value.rationale: The entry-minimum valuation is the canonical radical-filtration degree in every finite chain ring, and squarezero elements in the equal-Jordan-block centralizer form a natural nilpotent class. Uniformity across all nonautomatic shells is an exact structural cancellation valid in arbitrary residue characteristic and for equal- and mixed-characteristic rings. The formula gives a complete enumerator except only for the trivial unrefined automatic deep block, a closed-form total, and a nondegenerate limit distribution as ring length increases; it is not an arbitrary one-off small case or routine normalization.
